findings.summary: Page 1 packs three topics into one page and the reduce item mixes the fold concept with the init rule.
findings.evidence: "reduce((acc, x) => ..., init) folds an array into one value" / "Always pass init: empty array with no init throws TypeError"
findings.fix: Keep as is only if within block limits; otherwise move the init pitfall to its own labelled callout so the one-line idea stands alone.

findings.summary: The code block for map and filter appears before the one-line idea for the example is stated; the caption comes after the code.
findings.evidence: "javascript\nconst nums = [1, 2, 3];... same length vs shrunk to 0"
findings.fix: Put the caption 'same length vs shrunk to 0' before the code block, then show the code.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: rest syntax examples and the rule that rest must come last are fine, but the object-spread bullet and the example comment are separated from the code.
findings.evidence: "Object spread merges, later keys win" ... "// overrides.size replaces defaults.size"
findings.fix: Show the cfn/object-spread merge as a small before/after table (defaults, overrides, result) to make 'later wins' visible.

findings.summary: The deep copy bullets state structuredClone drops class prototypes and getters, but the comparison table omits these rows, and 'Functions' callout repeats the table row.
findings.evidence: "Drops class prototypes and getters" vs table rows Date, Map/Set, undefined, Functions, Circular
findings.fix: Add a 'Class instances | prototype lost | plain object' row to the table and drop the duplicate Functions callout text.

findings.summary: The Map vs Object table 'Order' row is unclear: the Object cell 'string keys, coerced' repeats the Keys row and does not state the ordering behaviour.
findings.fix: Change the Object cell to state the actual ordering (integer-like keys ascending first, then insertion order).

findings.summary: Quiz questions are followed by their answers and code in an order that puts the answer before the code the learner must reason about.
findings.evidence: "What do b === a and a print?\ntrue and [1, 10, 9]\n...const a = [10, 9, 1];"
findings.fix: Show the question and code first, then the answer and one-line reason.
